title: Top k by key
hints: heapq.nlargest(k, iterable, key=...) returns the k largest items ordered largest first and accepts a key function just like sorted().
Handle k <= 0 with an early `return []` so the answer is explicit rather than relying on library behaviour.
The full-sort alternative is sorted(items, key=key, reverse=True)[:k]. Both keep ties in input order; the heap wins on memory and time when k is much smaller than n.
